interactions.summary: The interviewer closes his empathy definition and Jiang signals agreement.
Jiang recasts the four-part empathy model as staged development from individualization into socialization.
The interviewer asks whether China's authoritarian and hierarchical social structure makes empathy-centered reform a major cultural shift.
Jiang agrees that unequal hierarchy is the core problem and says empathy, communication, and creativity all require more equal power, trust, and a politics not ruled by fear or face.
The interviewer asks what empathy development looks like beyond one progressive school and whether Chinese businesses or other schools are moving in that direction.
Jiang says empathy is the basis of effective schools, businesses, and societies because it channels everyone’s creativity, and he points to respected, anti-scientific-management tech firms as proof.

claims.claim: Jiang agrees with the interviewer's staged account of empathy and maps it onto an educational sequence in which people first become individuals and then learn to socialize properly with others.
Jiang says China lacks a culture of empathy because hierarchy and unequal power let the powerful bully the powerless.
He argues that communication requires equality, respect, and trust, and that creativity requires an environment where people are not afraid to make mistakes or offend superiors.
claims.temporal_scope: Current model of social conditions on 2012-03-16.

claims.claim: Jiang says China must re-examine its political system if it wants to progress as a 21st-century economy, society, and civilization.
He defines empathy at the institutional level as the ability of a school, business, or society to channel the creativity and energy of everyone involved into creating something great.
Jiang argues that firms which treat employees with respect and strip out scientific management thrive because they encourage people to act as creative individuals rather than managed animals.
claims.temporal_scope: Current business diagnosis on 2012-03-16 using contemporary tech-company examples.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang states the political-emotional core of the problem as the powerful feeling entitled to bully the powerless.
signature_moments.source_phrase: it is their right to sort of bully the powerless
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's bluntest condensation of why hierarchy destroys empathy in Jiang's account.

signature_moments.moment: Creativity is defined by the absence of fear: no fear of mistakes, no fear of offending superiors, no fear of losing face.
signature_moments.source_phrase: you're not afraid to lose face
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It connects creativity directly to the same anti-hierarchical atmosphere empathy requires.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang pushes the empathy discussion all the way into a demand that China re-examine its political system.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The packet escalates school reform into a civilizational and political argument.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's educational frame for the developmental step in which a person first becomes an individual before entering richer socialization with others.
Jiang's negative label for managing workers like controllable units instead of respecting them as creative equals.

chronology_notes.note: This packet anchors Jiang's 2012 position that China's educational and empathy crisis is inseparable from broader political hierarchy in the early 21st-century global economy.
